thread: Havel's help bends toward lanes he controls: careful local captain or something worse?

evidence.clue: Corin's flagged-shipment notices pile unread under the cracked river stone on Havel's table ('leave it with the others, lad, and I'll get to it'); the top sheets are in Corin's hand.

Havel routes the party to Fenner's by Hurdle Lane from behind, 'so it's covered. My lads walk Hurdle Lane day and night.' Sylvanas: the mill lane runs straight to Fenner's front gate; Hurdle Lane gives a back wall and little else; 'A captain who liked strangers kept on his own streets would send them that way.'

Count: 'Four, all told.' Havel named four yards on Mill Lane at the post and 'two I left out' (Kett's, the malt-house) only when asked about who took the new supplier's grain; Holt's 'you can leave out'; Garside's took a little and stopped.

He points past Tenter Row twice: 'Kett shut his gate at noon. You'll get nothing there tonight' and again down Hurdle Lane. Sylvanas: 'A man who knew his own streets and wanted a stranger on the ones he trusted would point like that. So would anyone who wanted her off Tenter Row.' Kett's is where the masked crew work. When she finds it: 'Kett shut his gate at noon. I'd have sworn to it.'
He offers Simmons's ladder at Fenner's loft; offers a cooper's doorway to stand in; a lad of his is there. His men watched the crew into the rope-walk (Cyndia).

At the table: dawn arrest with the magistrate's clerk with a lantern at the bend and lads at both ends of Tenter Row; Corin: they will be gone by then; Havel concedes the carts and re-proposes the same plan with spikes at the market gate and the shift-change arrest; he redraws the same chalk line down Hurdle Lane in the same groove three times; then asks for the Hurdle Lane end for his lads ('If it goes wrong, you'll want it shut behind you.').

Counterweight: his information is real (Mill Lane, supplier change, rope-walk sleeping); he did arrest two loaders at midsummer and the magistrate freed them by dinner; he keeps twelve men; Corin's 'it isn't four yards' he does not dispute. Sylvanas admits bias: she is sick of slow men; the Convocation would love him.

readerKnows: Havel's help is real and his steers are consistent; both readings survive on the page (careful, territorial captain; or something worse).
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas: 'wrong' with a documented bias beside it; she says nothing against him she cannot prove and watches his lanes rather than his words. Cyndia held him at the corner; Corin and Jaina have not voiced a suspicion.
notes: Ch8 reconciles. Guards: do not narrate him as cult-paid in Ch7; his formation question ('Who's on your back...') was held for Ch8; the rendezvous is the post (his ground), not one of his shelters.
